stories.title: Gloria Steinem, Influential Feminist Leader, Passes Away at 92
stories.summary: Gloria Steinem, a prominent feminist activist, journalist, and co-founder of Ms. Magazine, has died at the age of 92. Her foundation announced that she passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by loved ones. Steinem was a significant figure in the women's rights movement, advocating for gender equality and social justice throughout her life.

stories.title: Federal Judge Blocks New Executive Order on Birthright Citizenship
stories.summary: A federal judge has blocked the enforcement of a new executive order aimed at limiting birthright citizenship eligibility. The ruling referenced a recent Supreme Court decision that previously halted similar efforts to restrict citizenship for children born in the U.S. to parents without legal residency. Concerns were raised that the new order could potentially revoke citizenship from individuals already recognized as citizens.

stories.title: Leon Black Sues House Committee After Skipping Epstein Deposition
stories.summary: Leon Black, a billionaire and former associate of Jeffrey Epstein, did not attend a scheduled deposition before the House Oversight Committee. Instead, he filed a lawsuit against the committee, seeking to block subpoenas related to its investigation into Epstein. Black had previously been subpoenaed in June after leaving a voluntary appearance abruptly.

stories.title: Giorgia Meloni's Government Becomes Italy's Longest-Serving Since WWII
stories.summary: Giorgia Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office, making it the longest-lasting government in Italy's postwar history. This milestone surpasses the previous record held by Silvio Berlusconi's second administration. Meloni, Italy's first female Prime Minister, has governed since 2022, navigating both domestic and international challenges.

stories.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial Jury Continues Deliberations Amid Mistrial Concerns
stories.summary: The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial has returned for a sixth day of deliberations after previously reporting deadlock. The jurors have expressed difficulty in reaching a unanimous verdict, raising the possibility of a mistrial as Judge William Sullivan oversees the proceedings. The trial has garnered significant public attention since it began six weeks ago.

stories.title: Nvidia Acquires Hugging Face for $12.93 Billion
stories.summary: Nvidia has announced its acquisition of AI startup Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion. The company stated that it intends to maintain Hugging Face as an open platform, allowing developers to use it without being required to utilize Nvidia hardware. This move reflects Nvidia's increasing influence in the AI sector and its commitment to open-source technology.

stories.title: Nepal Flood Victims' Families Hold Symbolic Funerals Amid Ongoing Search
stories.summary: In Nepal, families are conducting symbolic funerals for their loved ones who remain missing following devastating floods that occurred last week. The disaster has resulted in over 1,200 confirmed deaths and left more than 4,000 individuals unaccounted for, leaving many families without the opportunity to perform traditional funeral rites.

Demonstrators criticized Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez for his government's handling of the situation, which has escalated following a surge in migrant crossings in July.

stories.title: Maduro and Wife Seek Dismissal of Drug Charges Based on Sovereign Immunity
stories.summary: Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have filed a motion to dismiss drug trafficking charges against them, claiming they are protected by sovereign immunity as the leader and first lady of Venezuela. They argue that this legal principle shields them from the charges of narco-terrorism and drug trafficking in a federal court.

stories.title: Maltese Tycoon Acquitted in Journalist Murder Case, Activist Expresses Devastation

Tom Gibson, Deputy Director for the Committee to Protect Journalists, expressed his devastation over the not guilty verdict, highlighting the ongoing struggle for justice in cases involving attacks on journalists.
